bullet_feedback.bullet: Implemented B+ tree and LSM-tree backends for the event log and benchmarked them on identical 2M-record workloads, where the B+ tree gave 12.8x the read throughput and 22x faster range queries at the cost of 27% more disk space
bullet_feedback.problem: Only bullet I could not restate without guessing: 'B+ tree and LSM-tree backends' and 'range queries' are opaque to a non-engineer, and the bullet never says what decision the comparison drove (which one was kept, or why the log needed storage at all).
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: I see three numbers (12.8x, 22x, 27%) but can't tell a hiring manager what was learned or chosen, so the bullet reads as a benchmark table rather than a win and I skip it.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: why the event log needed a storage backend, and which design was chosen as a result of the benchmark
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Lead with the purpose in plain words (storing the engine's event log on disk), then name the two designs as the comparison; drop one of the three ratios so the trade-off reads in one pass.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Cut AI workflow generation time 65% to under 15s by replacing a Claude skill’s open-ended search with focused sub-skills that call Python tools for workflow search and validation, guided by CloudWatch and OpenSearch latency logs
bullet_feedback.problem: 'Claude skill' and 'sub-skills' are product-specific terms; I understood the speedup but not what kind of thing was being sped up (a chatbot? an internal agent?). 'workflow' appears three times across 'workflow generation', 'workflow search' and 'validation'.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: The 65% is one of the headline wins, but a recruiter relaying it says 'made some AI thing faster' instead of something concrete.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: what the Claude skill is for users (e.g. an assistant that drafts test-data workflows from a request)
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Name what the AI feature does for developers in a few plain words before 'Claude skill'; move 'guided by CloudWatch and OpenSearch latency logs' earlier or cut it to the Skills section if space is tight.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Because the 270K+ row PostgreSQL workflow table had strict access limits, precomputed popular workflows into a category tree that the Claude skill searches first, with Redis caching full workflows to cut database queries
bullet_feedback.problem: No result or scale of improvement, and the sentence stitches three ideas (access limits, category tree, Redis) with 'with ... to', which reads compressed. 'strict access limits' is ambiguous: permissions or rate limits?
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: It reads as the 'how' of the previous bullet, not its own win; a recruiter will merge or skip it.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: whether 'access limits' means query rate limits or permissions
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Consider merging with the 65% bullet as its mechanism, or rephrase so the constraint and the fix read as cause and effect in plain words; keep 'precomputed popular workflows into a category tree' as the distinctive idea.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Writing Java logic that sets the upper and lower bounds on EC2 capacity that Amazon Redshift reserves for operations like patching, balancing availability against cost, and backtesting it
bullet_feedback.problem: The trailing 'and backtesting it' dangles after a long clause, so the sentence ends on an afterthought; 'Writing Java logic' is a weak opener for the top bullet on the page.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: This is the first bullet I read under the strongest brand; the clear idea (deciding how much reserve capacity Redshift keeps for maintenance) arrives late.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Reorder so the purpose leads (setting how much EC2 capacity Redshift holds back for patching and other maintenance), then the trade-off, then 'and backtesting the bounds against past data'; Java can move to the end or out.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Deployed a space-topic research tool for Amazon Leo’s public-policy team and set it up for handoff with AWS CDK infrastructure-as-code and GitHub Actions CI/CD, so Leo engineers new to the project now maintain it on AWS Fargate
bullet_feedback.problem: 'Amazon Leo' is not a name most recruiters know, and 'space-topic research tool' is vague about what the tool does. Tool names (CDK, GitHub Actions, Fargate) are spread across the sentence.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: The real win (a handoff that another team now owns) is good for platform roles but gets lost behind an unfamiliar client name and three product names.
bullet_feedback.missing_or_unclear: clarify: what the research tool does for the policy team in a few words
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Say what the tool does in plain words, keep the handoff outcome as the ending, and let one or two of the tool names carry the method.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Automated retraining for a production Amazon Bedrock classifier that rates research documents by importance: on an EventBridge schedule a larger LLM grades its ratings, and fine-tuning runs only when the grades shift past a threshold
bullet_feedback.problem: The colon splits the bullet into a headline and a mechanism, and 'a larger LLM grades its ratings' is a hard phrase to repeat out loud. No outcome stated.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: I understood it on a second read, which is one read too many in a queue.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Rephrase as one flowing sentence (a scheduled job has a larger model check the classifier's ratings and only retrains when they drift past a threshold); drop the colon.

bullet_feedback.bullet: Co-founded a 110+ member student product studio that has shipped 5 live products
bullet_feedback.problem: Doesn't say what Amar did technically as co-founder; it's a club stat, not engineering.
bullet_feedback.why_it_matters: Minor for infra roles; it does add leadership signal, but it's a line an infra hiring manager won't care about.
bullet_feedback.suggested_direction: Fine to keep as a one-liner; optionally merge into the role subtitle to free a line.

page_feedback.problem: Headline wins are not ordered for an infrastructure reader: the bolded numbers in the top half (90%, 65%) are about a developer tool and an AI assistant, while the most infra-shaped results (34% streaming latency, 1.26M events/sec) sit lower or unbolded.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: In a 7-second skim for an infra/platform role, I come away with 'AI tooling and full-stack' before 'systems and cloud pipelines'.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Reorder bullets within roles so the most infra-relevant win leads each one, and shift bold to the numbers that best support the infra story.

page_feedback.problem: The intended 'systems engineer who ships real systems' story is spread thin across five roles; the strongest systems evidence (order book) is at the bottom under Projects.
page_feedback.why_it_matters: A recruiter may stop before reaching the C++ project, which is the most distinctive systems signal on the page.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Keep the order but make sure the AWS and Kinesis lines read clearly as infra wins so the top half carries the story on its own; the UMIACS and TerpLabs entries could be tightened to bring the project higher.

page_feedback.problem: Almost every bullet runs to a full two lines, and several end on a trailing clause ('and backtesting it', 'to cut database queries', 'to reduce database load and latency').
page_feedback.why_it_matters: The page looks uniformly dense; nothing gives the eye a rest, and the ending clauses are what I skip.
page_feedback.suggested_direction: Trim one or two bullets to a line and a half by cutting tool names that the Skills section already lists.
